verdict.rationale: Nix's own documented features point toward third-party extensibility: users can create and build their own flakes, packages are addressed through named sources like `nixpkgs.some-package`, software can be installed over URLs, and Nix expressions can be turned into reusable functions. However, the pack never explicitly documents overlays, consuming third-party flakes/channels, plugins, or alternative backends, so extensibility is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of overlays or third-party flake/channel consumption, a plugin or backend extension mechanism, third-party binary cache configuration, and independent corroboration of the extension workflow.
